titles.title: Force de préhension et seuils de sarcopénie : valeurs de référence chez l'adulte, par âge et par sexe

descriptions.description:
Deux tables de référence sur la force musculaire, en format exploitable par machine.

 

force_prehension_centiles.csv, 36 lignes : centiles de force de préhension de 5 à 90 ans, par sexe, un point tous les cinq ans. Colonnes : âge, sexe, effectif, centiles 10, 25, 50, 75 et 90, moyenne, écart-type, unité, source. Valeurs en kilogrammes. Source : Dodds RM et coll., Grip strength across the life course, PLoS ONE 2014, 9(12):e113637, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0113637, tableau 2. Étude en accès libre portant sur 60 803 mesures auprès de 49 964 personnes, dans douze cohortes britanniques.

 

seuils_sarcopenie_ewgsop2.csv, 11 lignes : seuils du consensus européen EWGSOP2 pour le repérage de la sarcopénie, répartis en force musculaire, masse musculaire et performance physique. L'opérateur de comparaison figure dans une colonne séparée, pour que le seuil reste utilisable par une machine. Source : Cruz-Jentoft AJ et coll., Sarcopenia, revised European consensus on definition and diagnosis, Age and Ageing 2019, 48(1):16-31, doi:10.1093/ageing/afy169, tableau 3.

 

Portée et limites, à lire avant réutilisation. Ces tables ne posent aucun diagnostic. Un centile bas ou un seuil franchi justifie d'en parler à un médecin, rien de plus. Les centiles proviennent de cohortes britanniques, leur transposition à une autre population demande de la prudence. Pour comparer deux mesures d'une même personne, garder le même dynamomètre et la même position. Un erratum a été publié sur le consensus EWGSOP2, dans Age and Ageing 2019, 48(4), page 601. Nous n'avons pas pu le consulter et ne savons donc pas s'il modifie les seuils du tableau 3, à vérifier avant tout usage clinique. Aucun chiffre n'est de nous. Le travail s'est limité à transcrire fidèlement les publications citées, chaque ligne portant sa source.

titles.title: Bulgaria's clocks, 1979-1997 — with the Europe/Sofia chronology 1880-2026

descriptions.description:
Version of 6 October 2026: the correction is europe-sofia-1983-1996.patch, checked against tzdb 2026e, the newest release. The record and its page are updated: https://oco.bg/tz/sofia
Bulgaria's clock changes, 1979–1997, from the primary sources: the acts (Decree 6/1979 and Decree 94/1997 in the State Gazette; the Council of Ministers' decisions and protocols for 1991–1996 from its legal information system), the BTA notices of each transition in the Sofia dailies, photographed at the National Library, Sofia, and the chronology of every Europe/Sofia moment 1880–1997 with what each document says and the grade of what is held.

Version 2 (12 September 2026) corrects the patch of version 1: the autumn rule is the last Sunday of September at 00:00 for 1980–1996 (Decision 394/1995 and the BTA notice of 5 September 1989 put the 1995 and 1989 returns on the Sunday, not on 30 September as version 1 had them), and the 1979–1982 transitions — all at midnight in the 1979–1982 press — enter the patch. Added: the corrected patch (europe-sofia-1979-1996.patch), the correction letter to tz@iana.org, the nine acts as the Council of Ministers' transcripts (.doc), the September 1989 and September 1984 plates with their sunrise tables, and CHRONOLOGY-Europe-Sofia-1880-2026.md. Version 1's files are kept.

Version 3 (12 September 2026): the chronology runs to 2026 (the rule in force, ПМС 94/1997, witnessed by the Bulgarian Institute of Metrology's 2026 notice and the EU transposition register) and names the two instruments on order from the Central State Archive (Разпореждане 15/1980, Решение 196/1982); the correction letter updated to match.

Photographs: Ivan Petrov Ivanov, National Library "St. St. Cyril and Methodius", Sofia, 3–4 September 2026; camera originals retained with SHA-256. Evidence page: https://oco.bg/tz/sofia

titles.title: Sampling Thoughts During Music Listening
A Systematic Comparison of Probe-caught, Self-caught and Retrospective Thought Reporting Methods

descriptions.description:
This README file was generated on 6th October 2026 by Nao Toyama.




General Information 




Title of Dataset:  

Research Dataset for “Sampling Thoughts During Music Listening: A Systematic Comparison of Probe-caught, Self-caught and Retrospective Thought Reporting Methods.” 

 




Lead Researcher:  
Nao Toyama, Department of Music, Durham University 



Email nao.toyama@durham.ac.uk  




ORCID 0009-0004-6821-1784  

 




Date of Data Collection: 




18th February to 4th March 2026 




 




Location of Data Collection: 




Department of Music, Durham University, Durham, UK 




 




Brief Description of Dataset: 




This dataset contains raw and cleaned mixed-methods data collected for an empirical research project comparing thought sampling methods (probe-caught, self-caught, and control) during music listening. It includes survey responses (Qualtrics), codebook, and binary coding data from thematic analysis (NVivo). These files are formatted as .csv files prepared for statistical analysis in R.  






 




 




File Overview

Survey Responses (Qualtrics)  




Both quantitative (e.g., choice questions, scale-ratings) and qualitative (e.g., open-ended thought description) data were collected and then exported from Qualtrics. Participant ID (see Note for the definition and usage) was allocated in the first column of the cleaned data. As the online survey (Qualtrics) utilised loop and merge logic, several empty columns were generated; these redundant columns were removed during data cleaning. Furthermore, responses from participants who did not meet the pre-established inclusion/exclusion criteria (as detailed in the manuscript, see Appendix C: Data Screening), and the Qualtrics-generated timing data (e.g., first/last click, click count) were filtered out. 




 




Raw data 



Video_qualtrics_rawControl.csv

Video_qualtrics_rawProbe.csv

Video_qualtrics_rawSelf.csv





Cleaned data 



video_control_cleaned.csv 

video_probe_cleaned.csv 

video_self_cleaned.csv 


 




Codebook 








Codebook-final.pdf –– the finalised codebook revised through the Intercoder Reliability assessment, containing the updated hierarchical code structure, definitions, and verbatim examples.  






 

Binary Coding Data from Thematic Analysis (NVivo)  







Thought descriptions were extracted from the main Qualtrics dataset and imported into NVivo for thematic analysis using the Codebook. Each thought report was assigned a unique Thought ID (for its definition and structure, see Note). The qualitative themes coded in NVivo were then converted into a binary coding matrix (1 = present, 0 = absent) for statistical analysis in R, following these data cleaning procedures: 








Removal of unanswered entries: For the probe-caught group, participants may have skipped certain prompts (e.g., if Participant V3 responded to Prompts 1, 2, 4, and 5, but skipped Prompt 3). While such missing reports remain in the raw data, the corresponding unrecorded entries (e.g., V3_3D, V3_3P) were removed in the cleaned binary dataset to ensure complete-case analysis in R. 










Data Transposition for R Analysis: The orientation of rows and columns from the raw NVivo export was transposed in the cleaned version to format the data properly for statistical analysis in R (where rows represent individual thought entries and columns represent binary qualitative themes). 










Binary Standardisation (Recoding Duplicate Codes): In cases where a participant’s during-listening thought memo and post-listening thought descriptions on same occasion (e.g., V4_3D and V4_3P) were both assigned to the same qualitative code, NVivo originally exported a raw value of 2. Because these entries fundamentally describe a single underlying thought memo, all non-zero values were recoded to 1 to strictly preserve the binary definition (1 = presence, 0 = absence). 






 




Raw data 



video_coding_raw.csv 





Cleaned data 



video_coding_cleaned.csv 





 

 




Note 








Participant ID –– A single sequential numerical ID. This ID was generated by ordering the groups sequentially––probe-caught, self-caught, and control––and numbering participants consecutively from 1 onwards. It was assigned to all participants across all three groups, including the ones who did not meet the data screening criteria. Note that this Participant ID is utilised exclusively within the primary Qualtrics dataset.




Thought ID ––  A unique ID that has assigned to sach individual thought report––including blank or unanswered entries. Structure of this ID as follows: 














Group Prefix:  



V = Video (Probe-caught)

Vs = Video (Self-caught)

Vc = Video (Control)

















Group-specific ID: The number immediately following the group prefix. Participants were numbered consecutively from 1 onwards within each group. 
















Thought Indent & Timing: A combination of number and alphabet 



[N]D = [N]th thought report from the DURING-listening survey

[N]P = [N]th thought report from the POST-listening survey



Thought ID example: V1_1D means Video (Probe-caught), Group-specific ID 1’s 1st thought report from the during-listening survey.

titles.title: Chasse aux taxicabs : Travail de sape arithmétique sur cinq nouveaux 6-way dont 7-way dérivé
A Sieve-Theoretic Characterization of Splitting Factors for Taxicab Numbers via Eisenstein Integers
Entre le crible d'Eisenstein et le désert des reps "sauvages" : pourquoi les clefs de Boyer étaient les seules, et pourquoi le Graal reste hors de portée
Les taxicabs ne roulent pas sur toutes les routes - Preuve par convergence computationnelle que Ta(7) = BTa(7)
Titre original - Chasse aux taxicabs : cribles modulaires et facteurs de scission dans Z[ω]
14 nombres 5-way inédits exhumés, le noyau de Wilson scanné jusqu'à 48 millions, et deux théorèmes calculatoires d'absence renforçant Ta(7)=BTa(7)
Factorisation rétrograde du noyau de BTa(11), record de 21 splitting factors, et ouverture des soupiraux taxicab
Machine à Noyaux et Matrice des Valuations pour le Problème Taxicab

descriptions.description:
Cette campagne a essentiellement permis de mettre en évidence de nouveaux termes et des méthodes de recherche. Néanmoins, la preuve de minimalité, pour les bornes historiques tout comme ces nouveaux termes, demeure ouverte (bien que de nombreuses obstructions aient été établies dans ce travail et le dépôt suivant relatif à la géométrie elliptique sur les sommes de deux cubes). Honnêtement, pour le moment, je ne suis pas en mesure d'affirmer et produire les preuves complètes de minimalité pour les nouveaux spécimens comme pour les bornes historiques.

TITRE FRANÇAIS

Chasse aux taxicabs : cribles modulaires et facteurs de scission dans Z[ω]

TITRE ANGLAIS

A Sieve-Theoretic Characterization of Splitting Factors for Taxicab Numbers via Eisenstein Integers

RÉSUMÉ FRANÇAIS

Ce travail étudie les nombres de Taxicab et leurs facteurs de scission (splitting factors) à travers le prisme des entiers d'Eisenstein Z[ω]. Nous démontrons le Théorème du Crible dans Z[ω] : pour N = Ta(6) × p³, tout diviseur s se décompose sous la forme s = s₀ × pᵃ avec a ∈ {0,1,2,3}, et nous caractérisons exactement quand la représentation associée est primitive ou dilatée. Ce résultat implique une borne finie p ≤ 6773 pour les clefs de type a = 3 et une obstruction modulaire p ≡ 1 (mod 3) pour les clefs de type a = 0. Nous implémentons un crible prédictif exact qui identifie les quatre facteurs de scission de Ta(6) — {101, 127, 139, 727} — sans calculer aucune représentation, validé exhaustivement sur les 664 579 premiers p < 10⁷. Nous en déduisons que Ta(6) × 101³ = BTa(7) est le plus petit nombre à 7 représentations dans la famille cubique, renforçant ainsi la borne de Boyer (2008). Trois conjectures ouvertes sont formulées sur la raréfaction, le caractère cubique et l'unicité des facteurs de scission. Le dépôt inclut les codes sources Python, les jeux de données JSON et les manifestes SHA3-512 associés.

ABSTRACT ENGLISH

This work studies Taxicab numbers and their splitting factors through the lens of Eisenstein integers Z[ω]. We prove the Sieve Theorem in Z[ω] : for N = Ta(6) × p³, every divisor s decomposes as s = s₀ × pᵃ with a ∈ {0,1,2,3}, and we characterize exactly when the associated representation is primitive versus dilated. This result implies a finite bound p ≤ 6773 for type a = 3 keys and a modular obstruction p ≡ 1 (mod 3) for type a = 0 keys. We implement an exact predictive sieve identifying the four splitting factors of Ta(6) — {101, 127, 139, 727} — without computing any representation, exhaustively validated over all 664 579 primes below 10⁷. We deduce that Ta(6) × 101³ = BTa(7) is the smallest 7-representation number in the cubic family, reinforcing Boyer's 2008 bound. Three open conjectures are formulated on rarity, cubic character, and uniqueness of splitting factors. The deposit includes Python source code, JSON datasets, and associated SHA3-512 manifests.

MOTS-CLÉS FRANÇAIS

nombres de Taxicab, entiers d'Eisenstein, facteurs de scission, réciprocité cubique, théorie algorithmique des nombres, cribles modulaires, nombres de Hardy-Ramanujan

KEYWORDS ENGLISH

Taxicab numbers, Eisenstein integers, splitting factors, cubic reciprocity, computational number theory, modular sieves, Hardy-Ramanujan numbers

LICENCE MIT

RÉFÉRENCES CLÉS

Boyer 2006-2008 (Journal of Integer Sequences), Benfield 2024 (Ramanujan Journal), Monsky 2023 (arXiv), Dasgupta-Voight 2023 (arXiv), Ireland-Rosen 1990 (GTM 84), Ramanujan 1915 (PLMS)

NOTES

Couverture générée par Gemini Flash. Ce dépôt est le fruit d'une collaboration hybride humain-IA au sein du projet Cathédrale 1995. Forge.

EDIT V2 : Données étendues jusqu'à BTa(23) via Boyer et Wroblewski (Su 2016, OEIS A011541), avec factorisations vérifiées bit pour bit. Distinction de deux types de brisures dans la mécanique cubique : Type I (rupture de noyau, k=11, changement de courbe elliptique) et Type II (cube rationnel, k=19, courbe invariante). La Conjecture SRM v2.0 est précisée : k=19 n'est pas un seuil, le prochain seuil Type I est attendu vers k=29. Modélisation quadratique de la croissance : log₁₀(BTa(k)) ≈ 0,29 k² sur l'ère cubique k=6..23, avec prédictions falsifiables pour k=24..30 (BTa(24) ≈ 10¹⁸⁸). Le crible Z[ω] est réinterprété comme la filtration p-adique des points entiers sur la courbe elliptique Eₙ : le rank est invariant sous magnification cubique (E_{n·m³} ≅ Eₙ), seule la divisibilité filtrée prédit les splitting factors. L'infinitude des Taxicabs est un théorème (Fermat 1657, Hardy-Wright th. 412), non une conjecture ; seule la minimalité BTa(k) = Ta(k) reste ouverte. Deux courbes elliptiques couvrent toute l'ère cubique : Ère I (k=5-10, noyau 82652823799 contenant 1729) et Ère II (k=11-23, noyau 3956875867). Cinq prédictions falsifiables sont formalisées. Le document principal, ses codes Python, ses jeux JSON et ses manifestes SHA3-512 restent inchangés. Forge.

EDIT V2 (English) : Extended data to BTa(23) via Boyer/Wroblewski (Su 2016, OEIS A011541). Two types of ruptures in the cubic chain : Type I (core break, k=11, elliptic curve switch) and Type II (rational cube, k=19, invariant curve). SRM v2.0 refined : k=19 is not a threshold, next Type I threshold expected near k=29. Quadratic growth model : log₁₀(BTa(k)) ≈ 0.29 k² over k=6..23, with falsifiable predictions for k=24..30. The Z[ω] sieve is the p-adic filtration of integral points on Eₙ : rank is invariant under cubic magnification, only filtered divisibility predicts splitting factors. Taxicab infinitude is a theorem (Fermat 1657, Hardy-Wright th. 412) ; only minimality BTa(k) = Ta(k) remains open. Two elliptic curves cover the entire cubic era. Five falsifiable predictions formalized. Main document, Python code, JSON datasets and SHA3-512 manifests unchanged. Forge.

API freemium à venir après itérations et améliorations du travail.

Edit V3 visant les fichiers V301 et autres, PDF principal mis à jour : 

FR

Ce dépôt scelle la cartographie exhaustive des splitting factors de Ta(6) via le crible universel dans l'anneau d'Eisenstein Z[ω] et l'énumération des points entiers des courbes de Mordell associées. Nous démontrons que les quatre clefs de Boyer (101, 127, 139, 727) sont exactement les seules clefs splitting, établissant la complétude de la famille cubique à cet étage. Parallèlement, nous falsifions l'hypothèse du noyau cube-free et le critère de Monsky (I), et nous quantifions l'heuristique de Poisson sur les sauvages. La conjecture Ta(7) = BTa(7) reste ouverte : aucun sauvage n'a été trouvé, mais sa non-existence n'est pas prouvée.

EN

This deposit seals the exhaustive cartography of Ta(6)'s splitting factors via the universal sieve in the Eisenstein ring Z[ω] and the enumeration of integral points on the associated Mordell curves. We prove that Boyer's four keys (101, 127, 139, 727) are exactly the only splitting keys, establishing the completeness of the cubic family at this stage. In parallel, we falsify the cube-free core hypothesis and Monsky's criterion (I), and we quantify the Poisson heuristic on wild representations. The conjecture Ta(7) = BTa(7) remains open: no wild 7-way has been found, but its non-existence is unproven.

Édit V4 — Incise prospective : nous conjecturons que le théorème de structure du Crible Universel Z[ω] est transposable à d'autres anneaux cyclotomiques et équations diophantiennes. Nous esquissons des preuves de concept sur le problème de Sylvester (cubes rationnels) et les quintiques (sommes de deux 5èmes puissances), et évaluons honnêtement les murs théoriques et empiriques de cette transposition.

Edit V4 — Prospective digression: we conjecture that the structural theorem of the Universal Sieve Z[ω] is transposable to other cyclotomic rings and Diophantine equations. We sketch proofs of concept on Sylvester's problem (rational cubes) and quintics (sums of two fifth powers), and honestly assess the theoretical and empirical walls of this transposition.

Édit V5 :

Cette session ferme définitivement les familles cubiques descendantes des taxicabs historiques : aucun 7-way ne naît de cette généalogie, hors le chemin canonique Ta(5) → Ta(6) → BTa(7). Nous avons ensuite traqué les 7-way sauvages — ces nombres à 7 représentations primitives qui n'hériteraient d'aucun taxicab. L'exploration a révélé des créatures arithmétiques inattendues : des 6-way oubliés, et surtout des 3-way orphelins, baptisés les Faux Taxis Hors Piste, qui vivent entre Ta(3) et Ta(4) sans ancêtre cubique. Leur structure auto-suffisante — les normes x²−xy+y² ne consomment que les facteurs premiers de N — est inédite. titles.title: Data, Analysis Code, and Supplementary Materials for a Blinded Case-Based Comparison of Large Language Models and Urologists in BPH/LUTS Management

descriptions.description:
This repository contains the de-identified analytic dataset, correction/audit log, analysis code, reconstructed normalisation code, raw pre-normalisation responses, case-level answer key, and supplementary materials supporting the study entitled “Comparative Evaluation of Three Large Language Model Systems and Two Urologists in the Clinical Management of Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia and Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms: A Blinded, Case-Based Study.”

The study used 40 synthetic BPH/LUTS clinical vignettes answered by three large language model systems and two participating urologists. The responses were evaluated by two primary blinded urologist evaluators. The deposited materials are provided to support transparency and reproducibility of the reported analyses.

During revision-stage data verification, a source-attribution transposition between Urologist 1 and Urologist 2 was identified for Cases 25–28. The response texts and evaluator ratings were unchanged; only the attribution of these responses to the two urologist sources was corrected to match the original unblinding key. The final analytic dataset deposited here contains the corrected source attribution.

The normalisation code included in this repository is a reconstruction of the scripted component of the original workflow. The original normalisation procedure also involved manual review and editing and was therefore not fully reproducible from the reconstructed script alone. Details are provided in the accompanying supplementary materials and manuscript.

TITRE FRANÇAIS

Chasse aux taxicabs : cribles modulaires et facteurs de scission dans Z[ω]

TITRE ANGLAIS

A Sieve-Theoretic Characterization of Splitting Factors for Taxicab Numbers via Eisenstein Integers

RÉSUMÉ FRANÇAIS

Ce travail étudie les nombres de Taxicab et leurs facteurs de scission (splitting factors) à travers le prisme des entiers d'Eisenstein Z[ω]. Nous démontrons le Théorème du Crible dans Z[ω] : pour N = Ta(6) × p³, tout diviseur s se décompose sous la forme s = s₀ × pᵃ avec a ∈ {0,1,2,3}, et nous caractérisons exactement quand la représentation associée est primitive ou dilatée. Ce résultat implique une borne finie p ≤ 6773 pour les clefs de type a = 3 et une obstruction modulaire p ≡ 1 (mod 3) pour les clefs de type a = 0. Nous implémentons un crible prédictif exact qui identifie les quatre facteurs de scission de Ta(6) — {101, 127, 139, 727} — sans calculer aucune représentation, validé exhaustivement sur les 664 579 premiers p < 10⁷. Nous en déduisons que Ta(6) × 101³ = BTa(7) est le plus petit nombre à 7 représentations dans la famille cubique, renforçant ainsi la borne de Boyer (2008). Trois conjectures ouvertes sont formulées sur la raréfaction, le caractère cubique et l'unicité des facteurs de scission. Le dépôt inclut les codes sources Python, les jeux de données JSON et les manifestes SHA3-512 associés.

We deduce that Ta(6) × 101³ = BTa(7) is the smallest 7-representation number in the cubic family, reinforcing Boyer's 2008 bound. descriptions.description:
The Excel spreadsheet presented herein applies to the Portuguese territory, namely the Mainland and the autonomous regions of the Azores and Madeira. This spreadsheet is exclusively intended for the performance analysis of glazed openings and has been developed for research purposes to support the assessment of the energy performance of glazed openings in Portuguese buildings.

The applicable legislation arises from the transposition into the Portuguese national legal order of the European directives concerning the energy performance of buildings, namely Directive (EU) 2018/844, partially Directive (EU) 2019/944, and partially Directive (EU) 2024/1275.

The applicable Portuguese legislation includes the Building Energy Performance Regulation (DEE), approved by Decree-Law no. 101-D/2020 of 7 December, as amended by Decree-Law no. 11/2025 of 19 February. Energy performance was assessed in accordance with Order no. 6476-H/2021 of 1 July, as subsequently amended by Order no. 9216/2021 of 17 September and Order no. 12935-B/2023 of 15 December. The minimum requirements for the building envelope and technical systems are stipulated by Ordinance no. 138-I/2021 of 1 July. The Nearly Zero-Energy Building (NZEB) minimum energy requirements are established by Order no. 6476-E/2021 of 1 July. The regulation assumes a simplified method in a steady-state regime. The spreadsheet is intended for engineers, architects, energy experts and researchers involved in the assessment of building envelope energy performance under the Portuguese regulatory framework.

titles.title: Targeted, Genome-scale Overexpression in Proteobacteria

descriptions.description: Targeted, genome-scale gene perturbation screens using Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats interference (CRISPRi) and activation (CRISPRa) have revolutionized eukaryotic genetics, advancing medical, industrial, and basic research. Although CRISPRi knockdowns have been broadly applied in bacteria, options for genome-scale gene overexpression face key limitations. Here, we develop a facile approach for genome-scale overexpression in bacteria we call, "CRISPRtOE" (CRISPR transposition and OverExpression). We first create a platform for comprehensive gene targeting using CRISPR-associated transposons (CAST) and show that transposition occurs at a higher frequency in non-transcribed DNA. We then demonstrate that CRISPRtOE can upregulate gene expression in Proteobacteria with medical and industrial relevance by integrating synthetic promoters of varying strength upstream of target genes. Finally, we employ CRISPRtOE screening at the genome-scale in the model bacterium Escherichia coli and the non-model biofuel producer Zymomonas mobilis, recovering known and novel antibiotic and engineering targets. We envision that CRISPRtOE will be a valuable overexpression tool for antibiotic mode of action, industrial strain optimization, and gene function discovery in bacteria.

titles.title: Données et code de cryptanalyse computationnelle du cryptogramme de D'Agapeyeff (1939)

descriptions.description:
Ce dépôt contient les données brutes et le code source sous-jacents à une tentative de cryptanalyse computationnelle du cryptogramme-défi de 196 symboles publié par Alexander D'Agapeyeff en 1939, à la fin de la première édition de son ouvrage Codes and Ciphers (Oxford University Press). Ce cryptogramme n'a jamais été résolu. Ce jeu de données est le complément d'un rapport de recherche complet (méthodologie, résultats, discussion) documentant l'intégralité de la démarche ; il fournit tout ce qui est nécessaire pour vérifier, reproduire, ou poursuivre la recherche.

Le dépôt est organisé en quatre parties : le code Python de recherche (un script par hypothèse linguistique et par famille de chiffrement), les corpus d'entraînement et les modèles de langage qui en sont dérivés, les résultats bruts de chaque recherche effectuée (compressés, plusieurs millions de combinaisons journalisées), et l'état exact de couverture de chaque recherche au moment de son arrêt. Un manifeste détaillé de chaque fichier, sa provenance, et le format exact des résultats sont donnés dans le README qui accompagne le dépôt.

Quatre familles de chiffrement classiques (substitution, transposition columnaire, grille de Fleissner, double transposition) et un chiffrement Four-square par digrammes ont été testés systématiquement sous trois hypothèses linguistiques (anglais, français, hébreu translittéré), à l'aide d'un modèle de langage quadrigramme calibré et d'un recuit simulé. Chaque résultat a été confronté à une calibration par ligne de base nulle (la même recherche exécutée sur une version du cryptogramme mélangée aléatoirement, à volume d'essais égal) afin de distinguer un signal réel d'un artefact statistique produit par le test d'un très grand nombre de combinaisons.

À la clôture du projet, les méthodes A à D ont atteint une couverture garantie de 100 % sur deux balayages systématiques indépendants (run principal et calibration nulle), sans qu'aucun signal statistiquement distinguable du bruit ne soit détecté. Le chiffrement Four-square a été couvert à 20,9 % de son espace de recherche avant la clôture du projet, faute de ressources de calcul supplémentaires, sans qu'un signal n'y apparaisse non plus. Ce jeu de données documente donc un résultat négatif rigoureux, publié pour la transparence et pour permettre à la recherche d'être reprise exactement là où elle s'est arrêtée.

Les résultats bruts sous-jacents atteignent plusieurs gigaoctets et dépassent les limites de soumission d'arXiv, d'où leur publication ici plutôt qu'en matériel supplémentaire du rapport. Le code et les données sont publiés sous licence CC BY 4.0. Le rapport de recherche compagnon est en train d'être soumis à arXiv, mais déjà disponible sur Zenodo, lié à ce jeu de données. Une version anglaise de ce jeu de données et du rapport est publiée séparément sur Zenodo.

titles.title: Data and code of computational cryptanalysis of the D'Agapeyeff cryptogram (1939)

descriptions.description:
This repository contains the raw data and source code underlying a computational cryptanalysis attempt on the 196-symbol challenge cryptogram published by Alexander D'Agapeyeff in 1939, at the end of the first edition of his book Codes and Ciphers (Oxford University Press). The cryptogram has never been solved. This dataset is the companion of a full research report (methodology, results, discussion) documenting the entire investigation; it provides everything needed to verify, reproduce, or continue the search.

The repository is organized into four parts: the Python search code (one script per linguistic hypothesis and cipher family), the training corpora and derived language models, the raw results of every search performed (compressed, several million logged combinations), and the exact coverage status of each search at the time it was stopped. A detailed manifest of every file, its provenance, and the exact format of the results is given in the accompanying README.

Four classical cipher families (substitution, columnar transposition, Fleissner grille, double transposition) and a Four-square digram cipher were tested systematically under three linguistic hypotheses (English, French, transliterated Hebrew), using a calibrated quadgram language model and simulated annealing. Every result was checked against a null-baseline calibration (the same search run on a randomly shuffled version of the cryptogram, at equal trial volume) to distinguish genuine signal from statistical artifacts arising from testing very large numbers of combinations.

At the project's closure, methods A through D reached guaranteed 100% coverage over two independent systematic sweeps (main run and null baseline), with no statistically distinguishable signal detected. The Four-square cipher was covered to 20.9% of its search space before the project was closed for lack of further computing resources, again with no signal found. The dataset therefore documents a rigorous negative result, published for transparency and to allow the search to be resumed exactly where it left off.

The underlying raw results range up to several gigabytes and exceed arXiv's submission size limits, hence their publication here rather than as supplementary material to the report. Code and data are released under the CC BY 4.0 license. The companion research report is currently being submitted to arXiv, after what data will be publicly available. A parallel French-language version of this dataset and report is published separately on Zenodo.

titles.title: Perfect one-factorizations of K17,17 obtained from the K18 catalogue: 104,088 classes in canonical form

descriptions.description:
A catalogue of the perfect one-factorizations (perfect 1-factorizations, P1Fs) of the complete bipartite graph K17,17 that arise, by the K-construction, from the perfect one-factorizations of K18 with non-trivial automorphism group: 104,088 isomorphism classes, each given once in canonical form as a Latin square of order 17.

A one-factorization of K17,17 splits its 289 edges into 17 perfect matchings, called factors; written as a matrix with one side as rows, the other as columns and the factor number as entry, it is a Latin square of order 17. It is perfect when the union of any two factors is a single Hamiltonian cycle on all 34 vertices. Two factorizations belong to the same class when one is carried to the other by relabeling rows, columns and factors and possibly swapping the two sides, that is, by isotopy together with transposition; |Aut| is the order of the group of such relabelings carrying a factorization to itself.

The source is the complete catalogue of the 10,710 perfect one-factorizations of K18 with non-trivial automorphism group, doi 10.5281/zenodo.22238984, version 1.0.0. From a class F and a vertex j the K-construction (Laufer 1980; Wanless and Ihrig 2005) gives a symmetric Latin square I(F, j) of order 17 that is a perfect one-factorization of K17,17, and two roots give the same class exactly when an automorphism of F maps one to the other. Every class was folded at all 18 roots, 192,780 squares in all, each verified as a perfect one-factorization and brought to a canonical form; exactly 104,088 distinct forms result, in agreement with the count predicted from the orbits of the automorphism groups, and no form arises from two different K18 classes.

The catalogue is complete for these images and is not a catalogue of all perfect one-factorizations of K17,17: those from K18 classes with trivial automorphism group, and those not arising from K18, are absent.

The distribution by |Aut| is 2:84903, 4:18942, 8:205, 16:25, 32:11, 34:1, 9248:1. Two entries are atomic Latin squares, both previously published, and each is written out in full so the identification can be checked.

Two files: K1717_P1F_canon.txt, the 104,088 squares in canonical form, sorted and numbered, each header naming the K18 class and root it comes from; and K1717_from_K18.txt, the index from each K18 class to the roots that produce its distinct entries. The accompanying README documents the construction, the canonical form, the file formats, the entry numbering and the checks performed on the data.

titles.title: Check-digit error-detection rates: USCI (GB 32100-2015) vs VIN (49 CFR 565)

descriptions.description:
Detection rates for three transcription-error classes — exhaustive single-character substitution, exhaustive two-position transposition (bucketed by whether the check position is involved), and Monte-Carlo random double errors — measured over 2,000 generated codes per scheme with a fixed-seed PRNG. The USCI algorithm is the same implementation as this site's public checker; the VIN implementation was validated against the NHTSA manufacturer-handbook sample VIN.
Method, limits and the landing page: https://currawongweb.com/verify/check-digit-protection-study/

titles.title: Bulgaria's clocks, 1979-1997 — with the Europe/Sofia chronology 1880-2026

descriptions.description:
Bulgaria's clock changes, 1979–1997, from the primary sources: the acts (Decree 6/1979 and Decree 94/1997 in the State Gazette; the Council of Ministers' decisions and protocols for 1991–1996 from its legal information system), the BTA notices of each transition in the Sofia dailies, photographed at the National Library, Sofia, and the chronology of every Europe/Sofia moment 1880–1997 with what each document says and the grade of what is held.

Version 2 (12 September 2026) corrects the patch of version 1: the autumn rule is the last Sunday of September at 00:00 for 1980–1996 (Decision 394/1995 and the BTA notice of 5 September 1989 put the 1995 and 1989 returns on the Sunday, not on 30 September as version 1 had them), and the 1979–1982 transitions — all at midnight in the 1979–1982 press — enter the patch. Added: the corrected patch (europe-sofia-1979-1996.patch), the correction letter to tz@iana.org, the nine acts as the Council of Ministers' transcripts (.doc), the September 1989 and September 1984 plates with their sunrise tables, and CHRONOLOGY-Europe-Sofia-1880-2026.md. Version 1's files are kept.

Version 3 (12 September 2026): the chronology runs to 2026 (the rule in force, ПМС 94/1997, witnessed by the Bulgarian Institute of Metrology's 2026 notice and the EU transposition register) and names the two instruments on order from the Central State Archive (Разпореждане 15/1980, Решение 196/1982); the correction letter updated to match.

Photographs: Ivan Petrov Ivanov, National Library "St. St. Cyril and Methodius", Sofia, 3–4 September 2026; camera originals retained with SHA-256. Evidence page: https://oco.bg/tz/sofia

titles.title: A 55-Addition Rank-23 Scheme for 3×3 Matrix Multiplication — artifacts, verifier, and machine-checked proof

descriptions.description: Artifacts for the first 55-addition, 23-multiplication exact 3×3 matrix-multiplication scheme (previous record: 56 additions; Y. Sun, arXiv:2604.27645). The scheme uses ±1 coefficients, binary ± additions with free negation, no change of basis, and is valid over any ring (fully non-commutative; recurses on block matrices). Included: the explicit 55-operation straight-line program; an independent verifier (exact integer and non-commutative block trials, operation count); a runnable Rust transcription with fuzz tests against the naive 27-multiplication algorithm; a sorry-free Lean 4 + Mathlib proof that the program computes the matrix product over a general non-commutative ring; and the paper, which also proves that no 54-addition scheme exists anywhere in the published Heule–Kauers–Seidl catalogue (17,376 de Groote classes, every representative, every sign model). Developed in an extended interactive collaboration with Claude (Anthropic); every claim is mechanically checkable by the included tools.
